conviction_note: Little here is unpriced. The one real tension is guidance arithmetic. The FY 6.5-7.5% comparable-sales guide needs about 8.7-10.7% in H2 after 3.7% in Q1 and 4.8% in Q2, while the $12.97-13.0B Q3 revenue consensus implies only about 6-7% comparable. So a trim of the FY sales range is the most likely guidance event, but the street has partly priced it, and the -9.6 vol-point call skew says the options market leans up. The findings sum to -0.3. The scaled number is (2*0.48-1)*6.0 = -0.24, a near-coin-flip on a name whose last four prints moved 6-11%.
bar: Q3 adj EPS $1.42 consensus (Earnings Whispers https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/abt, whisper $1.44, revenue $12.97B; Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/abt/earnings $1.42), at the midpoint of company guide $1.38-1.46 (https://abbott.mediaroom.com/2026-07-16-Abbott-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-and-Raises-Full-Year-EPS-Guidance). Revenue consensus $12,995M (Hudson Labs https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/abbott-q3-2026-earnings-preview-abt-revenue-guidance-key-drivers). FY guide: comparable sales +6.5-7.5%, adj EPS $5.45-5.60. Sources agree, so the bar is sourced.
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.30% of float, 22.6M shares, 1.7 days to cover, Aug 19 2026 settlement (equibles https://equibles.com/stocks/ABT). No later settlement was found. Not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. The baseline's 25-delta skew is -9.62 vol points, so 25d calls are bid over 25d puts, an 'upside paid' lean. Put/call OI is 1.24 on the front expiry (10,820 total OI). The event-implied move is 5.53% against a 6.0% median of 7 prior reactions. Spot is 102.62: -21.4% from the 52-week high, +24.3% from the low, flat over 5 and 20 days. Sell-side: 33 Buy / 9 Neutral / 0 Sell, average target about $131 (fn2.ai, Oct 20 snapshot).

findings.finding: The FY guide sits above what the street models, so the sales range is likely to be trimmed. Comparable sales grew 3.7% in Q1 2026 and 4.8% in Q2, about 4.3% for H1. Holding even the 6.5% low end of the reaffirmed 6.5-7.5% FY range therefore needs about 8.7% comparable growth in H2, and about 10.7% for the top. Q3 revenue consensus of $12.97-13.0B, on a combined base of $12.24B (Abbott Q3 2025 $11.39B plus Exact Sciences Q3 2025 $851M), implies only about 6% reported. That is roughly 6-7% comparable depending on FX, against a Q3 2025 comp of 7.5% organic. If consensus is right, Abbott has to narrow or cut the FY comparable range on this print. If it prints 8%+ comparable, the guide holds and the H2-acceleration thesis is validated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has traded on the top line and the guide. Q3 2025 (-2.87%): revenue shortfall. Jan 2026 (-10.04%): FY guide disappointed. Apr 2026 (-6.0%): guide trimmed with the Exact deal. Jul 2026 (+10.71%): EPS raised, sales guide reaffirmed, comparable growth stepped up to 4.8%.
findings.source_date: 2026-04-16 (Q1 comparable 3.7%); 2026-07-16 Q2 release https://abbott.mediaroom.com/2026-07-16-Abbott-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-and-Raises-Full-Year-EPS-Guidance (Q2 comparable 4.8%, FY 6.5-7.5% reaffirmed); Hudson Labs preview (consensus $12,995M, Q3 2025 revenue $11,393M); EXAS Q3 2025 $851M https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1124140/000112414025000090/exas-20251103xex991.htm
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Consensus revenue already sits below the guide's implied H2 pace, so the street does not believe the top of the range. What is not visible is a stock trading as if a cut were certain. Spot is flat over 20 days, calls are bid (skew -9.6), and no preview found frames a sales-guide cut as the base case; previews repeat 'H2 acceleration' and the 'line of sight' language from the July call. If a cut were fully priced, put skew would be bid and estimates would sit at the guide's low end with commentary to match.
findings.independence: Three independent primary or secondary documents: the Abbott Q1 and Q2 releases, the Exact Sciences Q3 2025 8-K and the Hudson Labs and Earnings Whispers consensus. The arithmetic is mine. Against it: management said in July it had 'line of sight' to the H2 drivers (https://www.abbott.com/en-us/corpnewsroom/strategy-and-strength/abbotts-Q2-2026-earnings-call), and EP and Cancer Dx momentum could close part of the gap. Shrunk for the opposing call skew.

findings.finding: J&J's Q3 2026 release (Oct 13) shows its electrophysiology franchise slowing to +4.4% operational ($1,487M; US +7.0%, international +1.8%), from +5.6% for nine months and +12.6% in Q1. That is consistent with share moving to rival PFA systems. Abbott grew EP +13.4% comparable in Q2 (Europe >20%), guided EP to accelerate and outperform the market in H2 on Volt's full US market release in Q3, and received FDA approval for TactiFlex Duo (combined PFA/RF catheter) on Sep 8, 2026 with US rollout 'in coming weeks'. EP is about 6% of Abbott sales, so even a strong EP quarter moves total comparable growth by only about 0.3-0.5 points.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EP was cited as a share-loss drag in late 2025/Jan 2026 (stock -10% in Jan). Low-teens EP growth in Q2 was part of the +10.7% July reaction. No isolated EP-driven reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: J&J reported after Abbott last spoke, and its EP table sits in the supplementary schedules rather than the headline. A J&J deceleration does not show which rival gained (Boston Scientific's Farapulse is the larger PFA player and reports Oct 22, after this window). The read-across to Abbott is a proxy, and the international weakness (+1.8%) could also mean a softer EP market overseas rather than share moving to Abbott.
findings.independence: TactiFlex Duo approval: https://www.hcplive.com/view/tactiflex-duo-ablation-catheter-receives-fda-approval-for-afib (2026-09-08). Abbott Q2 EP +13.4% and H2 outperformance guide: https://www.abbott.com/en-us/corpnewsroom/strategy-and-strength/abbotts-Q2-2026-earnings-call. These are independent of the J&J document but Abbott's are company statements already public.

findings.finding: Q3 adjusted EPS bar is $1.42, the exact midpoint of the company's $1.38-1.46 guide, with a $1.44 whisper. Abbott beat by $0.03 in Q2 ($1.31 vs $1.28) and beat Q1 revenue by about $77M, and it raised FY EPS to $5.45-5.60 in July. An in-guide 1-2 cent beat is the base case and is inside what the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 EPS in line, stock -2.87%. Q2 2026 EPS +$0.03 beat with raise, +10.71%. EPS beats alone have not driven the reaction; the sales line and guide have.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The whisper ($1.44) already sits above consensus, so a 1-2c beat is expected. It is filed because the bar is confirmed, and it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: Abbott agreed on Sep 14, 2026 to pay about $385M ($348.7M federal, $36.3M states) to settle False Claims Act allegations over the Sturgis infant-formula plant, 2018-2022. It is a Q3 GAAP charge, almost certainly excluded from adjusted EPS, with no stated path to the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GAAP-only litigation items (Q2 2026 GAAP EPS $0.53 vs adj $1.31) did not stop a +10.7% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for five weeks and below adjusted operating income, so it is effectively priced. Filed for completeness at zero.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (Jul 16) CEO Robert Ford said nutrition was 'a little bit ahead' of plan and that Q3 should be the 'cleanest quarter' for the business before a tough Q4 comp. Nutrition was -3.6% comparable in Q2 and -7.7% in Q1 after Q4 2025 pricing actions, so a return toward flat or positive in Q3 is part of the H2 acceleration the guide needs. This lands inside what management guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nutrition weakness was part of the Q3 2025 (-2.87%) and Jan 2026 (-10%) declines. Nutrition beating expectations for a second quarter was part of the July +10.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Company commentary, public since July, inside its own guide. The counterparty check is not available: Danone reports Q3 on Oct 28, and Nestle's 9M release gives no infant-formula split. No independent series confirms or contradicts it before the print.
findings.independence: Q1 nutrition -7.7%: https://abbott.mediaroom.com/2026-04-16-Abbott-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results-Updates-Guidance-to-Reflect-Acquisition-of-Exact-Sciences. Q2 -3.6%: RTTNews 2026-07-16. Both are company documents, so there is no independent confirmation.

findings.finding: FX may hurt reported Q3 sales less than Abbott assumed. A secondary transcript summary says Abbott assumed about a 1% FX drag on Q3 sales. J&J's Q3 release shows only -0.3% FX on international sales and 0.0% on MedTech. If Abbott's FX drag comes in smaller than modelled, reported revenue and EPS against the $12.97-13.0B and $1.42 bars get a small cushion. Abbott's currency basket is more emerging-market-heavy (EPD in India and LatAm) than J&J's, so the transmission is a proxy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to FX alone. Comparable growth, not reported growth, is the line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts update FX in models, so this is mostly priced. The Abbott -1% Q3 FX assumption comes only from a secondary transcript summary (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/ABT/Q22026); the release itself gives no FX figure.
findings.independence: Proxy only. One peer document plus one secondary summary of Abbott's assumption.

findings.finding: In September 2026 a federal jury in the NEC infant-formula MDL (N.D. Ill.) returned a full defense verdict for Mead Johnson in the first bellwether to reach a verdict. Abbott faces more than 1,700 NEC suits, and a Missouri appellate court upheld a $495M verdict against Abbott in May 2026. A favourable MDL signal may draw call commentary that eases the litigation overhang on the multiple. It does not touch the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print reaction has been attributed to NEC litigation.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for weeks and about a peer, so mostly priced. Filed small because the call is the first time management can frame it.
findings.independence: Missouri $495M upheld: https://www.newstribune.com/news/2026/may/07/court-upholds-495-million-verdict-against-abbott/ (2026-05-07). That cuts the other way, and the finding is sized net of it.

outside_window.finding: Medicare coverage of CGMs for non-insulin type 2 diabetes. Abbott's CEO said in July it 'could happen in the fall' and called it a possible multibillion-dollar opportunity; Dexcom expects a CMS answer before year-end with coverage from mid-2027. No CMS proposal or decision was found as of 2026-10-20, and none is dated inside the window. Abbott may comment on the call, but the decision itself is not in the window.
Danone Q3 2026 sales (Specialized Nutrition, the infant-formula read-across) are due Oct 28, 2026, after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The lean is mildly negative on guidance arithmetic, against a call-bid skew (-9.6) and a flat 20-day tape. The skew argues the market expects the H2-acceleration story to hold, which is why the negative is shrunk and p_up sits at 48 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (sign against the skew): the guidance-arithmetic negative went from -1.5 to -1.0 because the -9.6 call skew says the market leans up. Short interest was checked (1.3% of float, 1.7 days to cover), so it is not crowded and there was no further squeeze cut. p_up moved from 47 to 48.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the EP finding went from +0.4 to +0.3 because EP is about 6% of sales.
Lessons 1 and 6 (inside the guided range): the EPS-bar finding went from +0.2 to +0.1 and the nutrition commentary from +0.2 to +0.1; both sit inside what the company guided.
Lesson 5 (proxy): the FX read-across from J&J went from +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 2 (one-off): the $385M settlement stays at 0; the NEC item stays small and is filed as 'other'.
Lesson 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct is kept at 6.0, the name's median reaction and above the 5.53% implied move, given a likely guidance touch.
